name: Cluster primes with complete even-difference coverage
description: construct() -> a prime p with 3<=p<=maximum=100000. Every positive even d<=p-3 must be a difference of two primes <=p. The evaluator independently checks all differences. Maximize p. Maximize a cluster prime at most 100000; every even difference through p-3 is checked using primes at most p. No density theorem or infinity claim follows. The optimum is 99991, the largest prime below 10^5, which is itself a cluster prime (OEIS A038134); this is a rediscovery task.

state_of_the_art.statement: 99991, the largest prime below 10^5, is itself a cluster prime, so it is the maximum. OEIS A038134 lists all 1807 cluster primes up to 10^5, and the count was recomputed here. Whether infinitely many cluster primes exist is Erdős Problem #17. Blecksmith, Erdős and Selfridge proved that they have density zero among the primes.
